method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the meningococcal chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Free to read, not CC BY; quoted with attribution. ⚠️ Treatment and contact chemoprophylaxis are in the CDNA guidelines, NOT retrieved.

claims.claim: ⚠️ ANYONE FROM 6 WEEKS OF AGE WHO WANTS TO REDUCE THEIR RISK of invasive meningococcal disease CAN RECEIVE MenACWY AND MenB VACCINES
claims.source_text: Any person who wants to reduce their risk of invasive meningococcal disease can receive MenACWY and MenB vaccines from as early as 6 weeks of age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: TWO VACCINE FAMILIES: MenB vaccines protect against SEROGROUP B; 3 MenACWY (QUADRIVALENT) CONJUGATE vaccines protect against A, C, W AND Y. ⚠️ Although RARE, IMD IS A SERIOUS INFECTION THAT CAN CAUSE SIGNIFICANT ILLNESS, DISABILITY AND DEATH
claims.source_text: serogroup B — MenB vaccines. 3 vaccines protect against meningococcal serogroups A, C, W and Y — MenACWY (quadrivalent) conjugate vaccines. … Although it is rare, IMD is a serious infection that can cause significant illness, disability and death.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: MenACWY IS FUNDED THROUGH THE NIP FOR ALL CHILDREN AGED 12 MONTHS. There are 3 MenACWY vaccines — MenQuadfi, Menveo and Nimenrix. ⚠️ INFANTS UNDER 12 MONTHS CAN RECEIVE ANY OF THE 3, WITH A PREFERENCE FOR MENVEO OR NIMENRIX; there is NO BRAND PREFERENCE FROM 12 MONTHS
claims.source_text: MenACWY vaccine is funded through the NIP for all children aged 12 months. … There are 3 MenACWY vaccines: MenQuadfi, Menveo and Nimenrix. … Infants aged <12 months can receive one of the 3 brands of MenACWY vaccine, either Menveo, Nimenrix or MenQuadfi, with a preference for Menveo or Nimenrix. There is no preference for brand of MenACWY vaccine – Menveo, Nimenrix, or MenQuadfi – for people aged ≥12 months.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: MenB IS FUNDED through the NIP for ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER CHILDREN UNDER 2 YEARS and for PEOPLE AGED 2 MONTHS AND OVER WITH CERTAIN MEDICAL CONDITIONS that increase the risk of invasive meningococcal disease
claims.source_text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children aged <2 years people aged ≥2 months with certain medical conditions that increase their risk of invasive meningococcal disease.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ MEDICAL CONDITIONS THAT RAISE RISK include COMPLEMENT DEFICIENCY (factor H, factor D or properdin), ⚠️ ACQUIRED COMPLEMENT DEFICIENCY FROM COMPLEMENT INHIBITOR THERAPY — ECULIZUMAB, RAVULIZUMAB OR PEGCETACOPLAN — FUNCTIONAL OR ANATOMICAL ASPLENIA INCLUDING SICKLE CELL DISEASE, HIV REGARDLESS OF STAGE OR CD4 COUNT, and HAEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANT
claims.source_text: complement components, including factor H, factor D or properdin deficiency people who may acquire complement deficiency after receiving complement inhibitor therapy (including but not limited to eculizumab, ravulizumab or pegcetacoplan) functional or anatomical asplenia , including sickle cell disease or other haemoglobinopathies, and congenital or acquired asplenia HIV, regardless of disease stage or CD4 + cell count haematopoietic stem cell transplant
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ HEALTHY INFANTS STARTING MenACWY AT 6 WEEKS TO 5 MONTHS: MENVEO OR NIMENRIX = 3 DOSES (8 weeks between the 1st and 2nd; 3rd at 12 months). MENQUADFI = 4 DOSES (8 weeks between the 1st, 2nd and 3rd; 4th at 12 months or 8 weeks after the 3rd, whichever is later). ⚠️ THE DOSE COUNT DEPENDS ON THE BRAND
claims.source_text: 6 weeks to 5 months Menveo a , Nimenrix 3 doses (8 weeks between 1st and 2nd doses; 3rd dose at 12 months of age) MenQuadfi 4 doses (8 weeks between 1st, 2nd and 3rd doses; 4th dose at 12 months of age, or 8 weeks after 3rd dose, whichever is later)
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ AT-RISK MEDICAL CONDITIONS STARTING MenACWY AT 6 WEEKS TO 5 MONTHS: ALL THREE BRANDS — MENVEO, NIMENRIX OR MENQUADFI — = 4 DOSES (8 weeks between the 1st, 2nd and 3rd; 4th at 12 months or 8 weeks after the 3rd, whichever is later). ⚠️ THIS IS ONE MORE DOSE OF MENVEO OR NIMENRIX THAN A HEALTHY INFANT GETS
claims.source_text: 6 weeks to 5 months Menveo Nimenrix MenQuadfi 4 doses (8 weeks between 1st, 2nd, and 3rd doses; 4th dose at 12 months of age or 8 weeks after 3rd dose, whichever is later)
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG ADULTS: a HIGH NUMBER OF CASES OCCURS AT 15-24 YEARS WITH PEAK RATES AT 18-20. They have THE HIGHEST RATE OF MENINGOCOCCAL CARRIAGE and are thought to play an important role in COMMUNITY TRANSMISSION. Higher-risk: people LIVING IN CLOSE QUARTERS, SUCH AS NEW MILITARY RECRUITS AND STUDENTS IN RESIDENTIAL ACCOMMODATION
claims.source_text: A high number of meningococcal disease cases occurs among adolescents and young adults aged 15–24 years, with peak rates of disease occurring in 18–20-year-olds. Adolescents and young adults have the highest rate of meningococcal carriage and are thought to play an important role in transmitting the bacteria in a community. … people who live in close quarters, such as new military recruits and students living in residential accommodation
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ BEXSERO AND FEVER: CHILDREN UNDER 2 CAN RECEIVE BEXSERO SEPARATELY FROM OTHER ROUTINE INFANT VACCINES, WITH A MINIMUM INTERVAL OF 3 DAYS, TO MINIMISE THE RISK OF FEVER — giving the routine vaccines first. Paracetamol is advised when Bexsero is given at the same time as other scheduled vaccines. MenB AND MenACWY CAN BE CO-ADMINISTERED AT ANY AGE
claims.source_text: paracetamol if they are receiving Bexsero at the same time as other routinely scheduled vaccines. … Children <2 years of age can receive Bexsero separately from other routine infant vaccines, with a minimum interval of 3 days, to minimise the risk of fever. In this case, give routinely recommended vaccines first. MenB and MenACWY vaccines can be co-administered at any age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: If possible, COMPLETE A MenACWY PRIMARY COURSE WITH THE SAME BRAND; if not, use an alternative brand following that brand's dose requirements
claims.source_text: If possible, complete the primary course of MenACWY vaccination with the same vaccine brand. If this is not possible, use an alternative brand following the dose recommendations by age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ EPIDEMIOLOGY SHIFTS: vaccination has SUCCESSFULLY REDUCED IMD FROM SEROGROUP C. IMD from SEROGROUPS W AND Y INCREASED FROM 2013 AND 2015, and MENINGOCOCCAL W HAS FALLEN since state MenACWY programs began in 2017
claims.source_text: Vaccination programs have successfully reduced the incidence of IMD caused by serogroup C. The incidence of IMD caused by serogroups W and Y increased from 2013 and 2015, respectively. However, the incidence of meningococcal W disease has fallen since state vaccination programs with MenACWY vaccine were introduced in 2017
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ CLINICAL FEATURES — THEY MAY BE NON-SPECIFIC. IMD usually presents as MENINGITIS AND SEPTICAEMIA, and SEPTICAEMIA, ALONE OR WITH MENINGITIS, CAN BE PARTICULARLY SEVERE. Features can include SUDDEN FEVER, RASH (PETECHIAL, PURPURIC OR MACULOPAPULAR), HEADACHE, NECK STIFFNESS, PHOTOPHOBIA, ALTERED CONSCIOUSNESS, MUSCLE ACHE, ⚠️ COLD HANDS, THIRST, JOINT PAIN, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. NOT ALL SYMPTOMS OR SIGNS MAY BE PRESENT
claims.source_text: Neisseria meningitidis can cause invasive meningococcal disease (IMD), which usually presents as meningitis and septicaemia. Septicaemia, either on its own or with meningitis, can be particularly severe. … The clinical manifestations of meningococcal septicaemia and meningitis may be non-specific.They can include: … sudden onset of fever rash (petechial, purpuric or maculopapular) headache neck stiffness photophobia altered consciousness muscle ache cold hands thirst joint pain nausea vomiting Not all symptoms or signs may be present
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ PUBLIC HEALTH: IMD IS NOTIFIABLE IN ALL STATES AND TERRITORIES. PROMPT DIAGNOSIS AND MEDICAL TREATMENT OF SUSPECTED CASES ARE CRITICAL. Public health authorities decide whether vaccination is needed for CLOSE CONTACTS such as household members
claims.source_text: Invasive meningococcal disease is a notifiable disease in all states and territories in Australia. Prompt diagnosis and medical treatment of suspected cases of meningococcal disease are critical. … The local, state or territory public health authorities will decide whether vaccination is needed for: close contacts of a meningococcal disease case,
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Meningococcal disease', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/meningococcal-disease, retrieved 2026-09-23
